title: Tekmar outdoor temperature incorrect or unstable
equipment: Tekmar 256 / 274 boiler controls (adapt for other models after checking their manual)

n1.text: Record the control model and current settings first. Does the control display an OUTDOOR SENSOR SHORT CIRCUIT or OPEN CIRCUIT error?

options.label: Yes, an outdoor sensor error is displayed
No error, but the outdoor reading is wrong or unstable

r_err.cause: The control cannot read the outdoor sensor, so it is assuming an outdoor temperature of 32 F (0 C) and continuing to run on that value.
fix: Short circuit: look for shorted wiring, moisture in the sensor or a defective sensor. Open circuit: look for a broken wire, poor connection or defective sensor.

Disconnect the sensor wires from the control, measure the actual temperature at the sensor, measure resistance, and compare with the manufacturer resistance chart (256 manual p.12; 274 manual refers to Data Brochure D 070). Do not apply voltage to the sensor.
On the 256, press the Item button to clear the error after repair. On the 274 the message self clears once the condition is corrected.

Verify recovery: confirm the outdoor reading is stable and plausible against an independent thermometer, review the reset curve and WWSD settings, then confirm boiler operation with the control's built-in test routine.

n2.text: Compare the displayed outdoor temperature with an independent measurement at the sensor. Is the displayed value steady but wrong, or does it jump around?

n3.text: Is the control set to use the outdoor sensor? (On the 274 the EMS / Demands DIP switch selects the tekmar outdoor sensor 070 or an external 0-10 V input.)

options.label: Yes, it uses the outdoor sensor
No, an external signal is selected, or unsure

r_stable.cause: The sensor, its wiring or its location is giving a consistently wrong value.
fix: Disconnect the sensor from the control. Measure the actual temperature at the sensor, then its resistance, and compare with the resistance chart. The sensor is a 10 kOhm NTC at 77 F; for example the 256 chart lists 13,474 Ohm at 65 F and 8,250 Ohm at 85 F.
Do not assume other sensor types share this curve; use the chart for the exact sensor model.
If the sensor reads correctly at the sensor location but not at the control, suspect the wiring between them.
A falsely high reading can place the control in Warm Weather Shut Down (256 manual p.8); a falsely low reading raises the boiler target.

Verify recovery: confirm the outdoor reading is stable and plausible against an independent thermometer, review the reset curve and WWSD settings, then confirm boiler operation with the control's built-in test routine.

r_jump.cause: An intermittent sensor or wiring fault.
fix: With the sensor disconnected from the control, resistance that is very high points to a broken wire, poor connection or defective sensor; very low points to shorted wiring, moisture in the sensor or a defective sensor (256 manual p.12).
Check every splice and terminal between the sensor and control, and the sensor housing for moisture.
Also check that sensor wiring is routed away from power wiring (general practice, not from the manual).

Verify recovery: confirm the outdoor reading is stable and plausible against an independent thermometer, review the reset curve and WWSD settings, then confirm boiler operation with the control's built-in test routine.

r_src.cause: The control may not be using the outdoor sensor you expect, or no value is being supplied.
fix: Check which outdoor input the control is configured to use. On the 274, the EMS / Demands DIP switch selects the tekmar outdoor sensor 070 or an external 0-10 or 2-10 V (dc) signal on terminals 2 and 3.
Check that the outdoor sensor is wired to the Com and Out terminals (274: terminals 2 and 3).
If an external signal is used, measure it at the terminals and confirm the source.

Verify recovery: confirm the outdoor reading is stable and plausible against an independent thermometer, review the reset curve and WWSD settings, then confirm boiler operation with the control's built-in test routine.
